agent.description: The SEAT this state is worked under, not the model build (RFC 1.4). Inherited by a returning agent; changed only for a genuinely different actor, with a DEC line naming both values. tools/validate.py rejects placeholders, `none` among them: 1.4 compares this field against itself to decide whether another agent is live, so an undefined identity makes the comparison meaningless in both directions. Where the FIRST seat name comes from at INIT is not specified by this schema and is open on the board -- this field records an identity, it does not derive one.

saipen_version.description: Protocol major version that wrote this state. Read from VERSION at checkpoint time.

schema_version.description: STATE file-format revision, integer. The current revision comes from this schema's x-current-schema-version metadata; revision 2 introduced the Core last_event checkpoint marker, revision 3 the style_contract voice marker. Any revision below the current one, or absence, remains readable legacy and WARNs, then MUST upgrade at the next checkpoint. Deliberately NOT in `required`: listing it there would hard-fail exactly the legacy states tools/validate.py must still open. Distinct from `saipen_version`, which is the protocol MAJOR that wrote the state.

saipen_home.description: RFC § 1.7's bootloader pointer: absolute path to SAIPEN home on the machine that last checkpointed.

execution_intent.description: The ONE canonical persisted execution-intent enum (RFC § 1.2, § 2.4). `normal` = ordinary one-step continuation; `goal` = an explicit user objective is running (the former `goal_mode: true`, safety-valve counters `goal_waves`/`goal_tickets` REQUIRED and bound to this value); `converge` = bare `cc` continuation to closure with no new objective. The legacy `goal_mode` boolean remains READ-compatible only during migration: `true` maps to `goal`, `false` to `normal`. A state carrying BOTH this field and `goal_mode` is corrupt -- tools/validate.py FAILs it, because after the first canonical checkpoint there is exactly one source of truth.

goal_mode.description: LEGACY field. Read-compatible during migration only: `goal_mode: true` maps deterministically to `execution_intent: goal`, `false` to `normal`. The next checkpoint MUST drop this field and write `execution_intent`. A state carrying both is corrupt (tools/validate.py FAILs it).

goal_waves.description: Safety-valve counter, RFC § 2.4. MUST be present when execution_intent is `goal`, MUST be absent otherwise.

goal_tickets.description: Safety-valve counter, RFC § 2.4. MUST be present when execution_intent is `goal`, MUST be absent otherwise.

last_event.description: Numeric N from the highest E-N event in the Core LOG at the checkpoint that produced this STATE. REQUIRED by tools/validate.py when schema_version is 2 and LOG contains an event; omitted only for a fresh empty LOG or readable legacy v1 state. Kept out of the JSON Schema `required` array because that array cannot express either condition.

style_contract.description: RFC § 1.2's voice marker: the `ded-XXXXXXXX` token declared at the top of saipen/STYLE.md, derived from that file's own text. REQUIRED by tools/validate.py when schema_version is 3, omitted only in readable legacy state below that revision. Kept out of the JSON Schema `required` array for the same reason as last_event: the array cannot express the condition. It is last_event's shape applied to the one contract nothing could witness -- a value whose truth lives in a file outside STATE, so a checkpoint that never opened STYLE.md cannot write it correctly and cannot stay silent about that.

human_note.description: Optional one-line human->agent nudge, read on continue (RFC § 1.2) and cleared once applied. Not a ticket, not a goal.

transition_from.description: The phase this state transitioned FROM. REQUIRED on every state except a fresh INIT -- part of RFC § 1.2's required set, which is the normative list; this file is its machine-readable mirror, never a second opinion about it. Deliberately NOT in `required`: that array cannot express 'except fresh INIT', and listing it there would hard-fail exactly the bootstrap state RFC § 1.2 exempts -- the same reason schema_version is kept out. The conditional is enforced in tools/validate.py instead (FAIL when phase is not INIT, WARN when it is), so absence from `required` here means 'checked elsewhere', never 'optional'. Combined with `phase` to validate transitions against RFC § 1.6. A fresh INIT bootstrap may set transition_from: INIT (self-referential, logically 'came from nothing').
